input.quote: Neither Party may terminate this Agreement during the Initial Term except as set forth in paragraph 4(b) or any Exhibit. Either Party may terminate this Agreement for any reason following the Initial Term upon ninety (90) days written notice to the other Party. Except for termination for material breach as detailed in paragraph 4(b), Kubient shall be entitled to all fees generated during the termination period regardless of which Party terminates the Agreement
input.rationale: Clause 4(a) sits at the playbook fallback and is therefore acceptable without redline. The Initial Term is one (1) year — not a multi-year commitment — so the absence of a convenience right during that period does not trigger the "missing behaviour" deviation (which applies to terms longer than 12 months), and thereafter AP may terminate for any reason on ninety (90) days' notice, i.e. within the fallback's 60–90 day window. There is no early-termination fee or acceleration: under clause 5 AP pays no fees at all (revenue share flows from Kubient to AP), and Kubient's entitlement to "all fees generated during the termination period" is simply its continuing revenue share on impressions actually monetised during the notice period, not a penalty, so there are no prepaid fees to refund. On Kubient's side, its convenience right also requires ninety (90) days' notice and cannot be exercised during the Initial Term, so the walk-away trigger (vendor convenience on fewer than 90 days' notice) is not met. Two sub-elements fall short of the preferred position and are noted rather than flagged: AP's notice period is 90 days rather than 30, and Kubient's convenience right is not expressly confined to the end of a renewal term. If the term is later extended beyond one year or renewal terms are lengthened, we should revisit and add a 30-day AP convenience right with a pro-rata refund mechanic.
